title: dispatch prepare --claim registers the execution worker it claims for
action: Friction rows 670/707: a cell claimed via `bee dispatch prepare --claim` is claimed WITHOUT its worker being registered, so `cells finish` on a small+ lane later refuses at the B44 registered-worker door and the remedy is a manual `state worker add`. Fix: in the prepare driver, after a SUCCESSFUL claim, register the claimed-for worker against the cell in the same call — same record shape as `state worker add --nickname <worker> --cell <id> --tier <tier> --status running` (reuse the existing worker-add code path, never a parallel writer; locate it under verbs/state_group/ — the declared read_first dir is a starting point, follow the real module). Tier comes from the cell's own tier field, defaulting as state worker add defaults. Rules: no registration when --claim absent; no registration when the claim itself fails; if the claim succeeds and the registration then fails, the payload and text output say so loudly (claim stands, registration_error named) — never silent. Payload gains a worker_registered: true|false field on the claim branch. TDD: red test first proving prepare --claim leaves a registered worker findable by the same read the B44 door uses; tests for claim-failure (no registration), no --claim (no registration), and the registration shape (nickname/cell/tier/status). Keep every existing prepare and worker test green.

truths: a prepare --claim leaves the worker registered for the cell (B44 door finds it)
a failed claim or a claim-less prepare registers nothing
registration failure after a successful claim is loud in payload and text

artifacts.substantive: registration wiring plus tests, no TODO stubs

trace.outcome: prepare --claim registers the claimed worker through the shared worker-add path; payload carries worker_registered/registration_error; failed or absent claim registers nothing
